name: Nüchuang
description: A star 115 parsecs away, 68 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 84380: radius 67.631 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 1255.76 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.061) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 84380: effective temperature 4181 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.116)

gravity.source: SIMBAD's compilation of spectroscopic measurements (mesFe_h): log g 1.78 from 2023ApJS..266...41P; the 12 published values span log g 1.42 to 4.1, across which the limb law changes by at most 2.6% of the centre brightness

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 84380: distance 115.473 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.014), at which the luminosity and radius hold

text.card: A star 115 parsecs away, 68 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 1,256 times the Sun's luminosity at 4,181 K, so 67.631 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 84380: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Pi Herculis
quotes.card: Pi Herculis, Latinized from π Herculis, formally named Nüchuang, is a third-magnitude star in the constellation Hercules.
quotes.introduction: As one of the four stars in the Keystone asterism, specifically representing the northeastern corner, it is one of the constellation's more easily recognized.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 1339952869195300608 (quality A), from 2005A&A...430..165F; Gaia DR3 measures none
